posts.title: Americanism Redux: November 26, Your Today, 250 Years Ago, In 1776
posts.description: Americanism Redux: Your Today, November 26, On The Journey to the American Founding, 250 Years Ago, In 1776 You’re in a boat and you’re taking on water. No denying it. The only question is how many holes there are. If it’s one, a patch could work. If it’s ten, abandonment is probably the only option. Defeat is a lot like that leaky boat. One defeat is manageable. You can handle it. But ten, and all at what feels like once? That’s not defeat anymore. That’s futility, with just one thing left to say: Abandon ship. You’re in Americanism Redux, 250 years ago today, with the boat filling up and the future feeling sopping wet. * * * * * * * (a bridge still up on the Passaic) Okay, we’re done. Back in formation. Feet soaking wet from the frigid water and cold mud. Clothes that were already threadbare and stinking are more so now. Several men are barefoot. posts.title: Americanism Redux: Your Today, November 19, 250 Years Ago, In 1776
posts.description: Americanism Redux: Your Today, November 19, On The Journey to the American Founding, 250 Years Ago, In 1776 Simple as simple gets. Hardly anything simpler when you look at it. X—Y…Z. “X” is you deciding, your decision. “—” time elapsed. Short, long, whatever, the time since deciding. “Y” is the result, not reaction and not response, but the result from your decision, for you and for others. “…” another elapsing of time, open toward the future but with an end in mind. “Z” is the next, the end reached, the future halted as the present restarts. This is the today of 250 years ago and you are in Americanism Redux. * * * * * * * (site of the tragedy) Three days ago, Nathanael Greene’s decision was to hold Fort Washington with his nearly 3,000 men. His decision, no one else’s. Given the leeway by his boss, General George Washington, who also advised at the same time against doing it, Greene made the final call. Hold the fort. Pass the word. posts.title: Americanism Redux: November 12, Your Today, 250 Years Ago, In 1776
posts.description: Americanism Redux November 12, your today, on the journey to the American Founding, 250 years ago, in 1776 Two options in front of me. Both make sense and a case can be made for each. I choose one of them. And now, because of my choice, here we go, in this direction, with no turning back. Welcome to today, 250 years ago, and to Americanism Redux. * * * * * * * (go catch one) A pond is not far from here. The pike are biting. Take a pole and do some fishing. The burdens, the grind, will just disappear, at least for a while. Well deserved. That’s the advice one of Nathanael Greene’s followers has given to him. 34 years old, a Rhode Islander, one-time Quaker, and prone to walking with a limp, Greene is a Continental Army General and a member of General George Washington’s “core team”. He’s also serious-minded, open to new ideas, and skilled at learning; what he’s “read and heard about” is the foundation of his rise to his current position of military leadership.
